outcome_detail: Per Tate Record reporting dated June 17, 2026, the City of Senatobia and Police Chief Richard Chandler were cleared/dismissed from the $10 million federal lawsuit. The disposition of the claims against Officer Willis McNeil individually is not stated in accessible coverage. No settlement or plaintiff recovery was reported.
criminal_detail: No criminal charges against Officer Willis McNeil were reported in available coverage. At filing, the plaintiff's attorney publicly said he wanted McNeil prosecuted for sexual battery, but no charging decision was found in later reporting.
incident_date_approx: August 25, 2023, near Senatobia/Sardis, Tate County area, Mississippi
description: A woman filed a federal civil rights lawsuit on May 21, 2024, in the Northern District of Mississippi against the City of Senatobia, Police Chief Richard Chandler, and Senatobia Police Officer Willis McNeil, seeking $10 million in damages. According to the complaint, on August 25, 2023, the woman was a passenger in a vehicle stopped by a Sardis police officer; the suit alleges Officer McNeil then arrived, detained her without cause, drove her to a wooded area, turned off his body camera, and sexually assaulted her. The suit brought counts including excessive force, false arrest and imprisonment, assault and battery, and negligence against the officer, and failure to train and supervise against the city and chief, who called the allegations blatantly false. Local reporting in June 2026 stated that the city and the police chief had been cleared in the case.
